title: QuADMESH+: Quadrangular ADvanced Mesh generator
description:
QuADMESH is a Python port of QuADMESH+ (Mattioli, 2017, QuADMESH+: A Quadrangular ADvanced Mesh Generator for Hydrodynamic Models, master's thesis, The Ohio State University). It converts an existing triangular mesh for a two-dimensional shallow-water model into quadrilaterals by merging adjacent triangle pairs, one element layer at a time from the boundary inward. The conversion reuses the input vertices, leaves no interior residual triangle, and returns a quad-pure mesh by default; it adds points only to clear leftover boundary triangles. Mesh layers, smoothing and quality metrics come from CHILmesh. The entry point is tri2quad, with a command-line interface in quadmesh.cli. Install with pip install quadmesh; the import name is quadmesh.

This release (0.2.5)

Fixed

  • The per-layer sweep now treats layer 0 as the boundary layer, as in CHILmesh and the MATLAB code; it used the innermost layer. Mean skew on the bundled structuredMesh1 changes from 0.696 to 0.647.
  • fem_smoother restores every boundary vertex to its exact coordinates after each pass.

Added

  • preserve_boundary (CLI --preserve-boundary, default off): boundary-quad cleanup keeps every original boundary vertex. On the four bundled meshes, vertices lost fall from 2 to 18 per mesh to 0, at a cost of 1 to 9 extra elements.
  • quadmesh-bench: compares QuADMESH+ with other triangle-to-quad methods, including Gmsh Blossom-Quad and QuadriFlow when installed.
  • n_concave in the quality statistics, and docs/algorithm.md, which sets the thesis algorithm against the port.

Changed

  • Requires chilmesh>=1.5.5. Test meshes come through Valence via chilmesh.registry, pinned by SHA-256.
  • Ethan J. Kubatko is listed as second author.

Known limitation: some boundary-layer quads can be concave.
